summary: Frederick County, MD: a 1920 steel lookout was rebuilt on its site as a 100-foot tower in 1951, which collapsed in a 1976 windstorm; no source read describes the site today.

facts.design: 100-foot all-steel tower on a concrete base with a 7-by-7-foot cab (1951)
facts.status_note: Collapsed in a strong wind gust in October 1976

staffing.status: manned on and off; last named towerman in sources read is Andrew H. Abraham (1955)

corrections.why: The 1951 tower that the record dates is described as 100 feet (about 30.5 m) high. 18.3 m is 60 feet, the height the 1928 newspaper gives for an earlier tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 47 feet (the 1918-19 state plan and the 1951 article), 50 feet (the 1930 state report) and 60 feet (the 1928 newspaper). The 1951 tower was 100 feet.
Two towers carried the Foxville name: a steel tower completed in 1920 and the 100-foot tower built on its site in 1951. The record's 1951 build date belongs to the second.

notes_for_editor: History is well sourced from transcribed state reports and newspapers, but the sources give three different heights for the 1920 tower. Site today: no source read says what remains or whether the spot is public; a field check or Maryland DNR records would settle it. The brief's FFLOS registration date (2016) is visible in the cached register text as 'Date Registered November 27, 2016'; the story does not use it. The brief's 1976 'removed' is recorded as destroyed (collapsed). The 1918 Sand Flats lookout is background only and may be a different site; the story says the sources do not say whether the steel tower replaced it. An NPS Catoctin resource-study appendix mentions a 'Foxville Watch Tower' photo from about 1915; it appeared in search only and was not read or added.
